mainEntity.name: What is negative air vacuum trunk line cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Negative air vacuum trunk line cleaning is an engineered HVAC decontamination method that uses high-volume commercial extractors to place an entire ventilation network under continuous negative pressure. While the vacuum pulls airborne particulates toward high-efficiency HEPA filters, technicians mechanically agitate duct interiors, ensuring extracted debris cannot escape into indoor living spaces.

mainEntity.name: Why is household or shop vacuum duct cleaning ineffective?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard household and portable shop vacuums produce less than 150 CFM of airflow, which is completely inadequate to lift settled debris inside large twelve-inch galvanized trunk lines. Furthermore, standard vacuums lack sealed HEPA containment, causing fine sub-micron dust and mold spores to exhaust directly back into your home through the vacuum exhaust port.

mainEntity.name: How much airflow capacity is required for whole-home negative air cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Professional whole-home trunk line cleaning requires between 3,500 and 5,000 CFM of negative airflow capacity. This volume creates high-velocity air movement across the entire cross-section of main trunks, keeping heavy dust particles suspended in the airstream until they reach the primary filtration chamber.

mainEntity.name: Will negative air duct cleaning make a mess in my living areas?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Because the ventilation system operates under continuous negative pressure during cleaning, air is constantly drawn inward from your living spaces into the ductwork. Even if a register cover is removed, room air rushes into the vent rather than blowing dust out, guaranteeing spotless living spaces with zero blowback.

mainEntity.name: Do technicians need to cut access holes in the ductwork?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. NADCA ACR 2021 standards require cutting temporary access ports into the main supply and return trunks close to the furnace plenum to connect high-volume vacuum collars. Upon service completion, these openings are permanently sealed with heavy 26-gauge galvanized steel patch plates, self-tapping screws, and foil mastic tape.

mainEntity.name: How long does a complete negative air trunk cleaning appointment take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A comprehensive negative air cleaning appointment for an average Rockford single-family home typically takes three to four hours. This timeframe allows our two-technician crew to seal all registers, establish negative vacuum containment, pneumatically sweep every supply and return branch, and complete visual camera inspection passes.
